## Generated Dialogue Scripts: English Transcript Rendering

This file preserves the extracted English rendering of the generated paired dialogue scripts. It is not the authoritative Japanese material that was rated. The authoritative script files are the Japanese CSV files in `data/counseling_scripts/scripts/`, with metadata and file mapping in `data/script_inventory/analysis_script_list_v1.0.csv`. Each pair was reconstructed from one dynamic session-generation run for the same client condition and generation replicate. During the dynamic run, each counselor turn proceeded from shared Layers 1-2 processing to a Layer 3 draft and then to a Layer 4 final response; the client agent then responded to the Layer 4 final response. The Layer 3 draft was retained but was not sent to the client agent.

Consequently, the paired scripts share the same client utterance sequence and the same Layer 4-conditioned session trajectory. The Layer 3 draft-rendering script combines those shared client utterances with the retained Layer 3 draft counselor responses, whereas the Layer 4 final-rendering script combines the same client utterances with the Layer 4 final counselor responses. The pairing documents the materials used for the response-rendering comparison; it should not be interpreted as a pair of independently generated Layer 3-only and Layer 4-only dialogue trajectories, nor as a test of whether adding Layer 4 improves downstream session trajectories or primary outcomes.

The transcript headings below follow this order: situation condition, PERMA profile, response-rendering label, and generation number. Line breaks, blank cells, spacing, and extraction artifacts in this rendering are preserved for auditability and should not be treated as corrected transcript text.

1         counselor       Thank you for sharing that. As a section chief in sales administration, it sounds like you are
                          having a hard time because you keep thinking about tomorrow’s plans at night, and when
                          your subordinates’ mistakes and instructions from above pile up, you get irritated and end
                          up speaking harshly. Here, you can talk about those sleepless nights and the situations that
                          make you irritated at a pace that feels manageable. You can decide for yourself where to
                          start and how to talk about it.

                          pattern out of my head, and it bothers me even before I go to sleep.
3         counselor       Even in your anxiety, you are trying to put those sleepless nights into words and share

                          that repeating pattern.
4         client          Even tonight, even when I lie down, I keep turning over tomorrow’s plans and cannot sleep.

                          time,” in a harsh way. I still cannot sort out what I feel or how I should talk about it, and I

5         counselor       It may be that, while you are holding on to that scene from this morning’s meeting where
